Actors Who Hate Their Own Movies
It's interesting to come across this today. Last night I watched Airport (1970) and the IMDB trivia reports that Burt Lancaster called it "the worst piece of junk ever made." FWIW I enjoyed it...
Also, mechanics of Voat, which cars have you seen most frequently in your shop, and what was typically the nature of the repairs?
Of the cars you have driven or worked on, which cars are your favorites, and which are your least favorites?

By far the easiest to work on was my '89 2WD Toyota pickup. It had NO options, carbureted, manual steering, no A/C, etc, etc. The only accessories on the engine were the water pump and alternator. The engine bay was built around being able to fit a V6, so there was plenty of room around the 4-cylinder. Everything was super easy to get to, 95% or more of the fasteners are either 12, 14, or 17mm, parts were cheap and plentiful. My other '70s/'80s RWD Toyotas were all equally a joy to work on, just a little less space under the hood.

Not sure hardest that I've actually worked on, but I have a V8 BMW now that I wouldn't even consider working on myself. That engine is just crammed in there and I think you'd have to dismantle half of it just to fit your hand past the heads. Computer-controlled everything, which I'm not opposed to, just not really set up to work with.

Drove a Ferrari F430 at a track day. That was pure joy. It goes exactly where you tell it but it doesn't give you a lot of warning that you are pushing too hard. Had a big moment on my 3rd lap because I got cocky.

Worst? Honda Insight. Slow, loud, and ugly. But it was good on gas.

My 86 GTI was really easy to work on, it was ok to drive. It was an 8v, so it wasn't as fast as the 16v, but it handled pretty well. I currently own a Golf R, it's ok, but I prefer my F-250 diesel, or my VFR 800. the VFR FFLLIIEESS!
least favorite to work on: 2001 Subaru Outback VDC. cramming a flat 6 into a place designed for a flat 4 is just a disaster.

Ooo, that sounds rough. Its not much easier with a 4 cylinder. Had to replace a clutch. Its terrible! You have the engine and transmission all reassembled on a hoist and you want to drop it back in, but the angle is impossible!

1998 E320 Mercedes - This car is a dream to drive. Very responsive, with a switch that chooses whether you want it to start in second gear ('W' - Presumably for Winter, or something) or in first gear ('S' - presumably for Summer or Sport...I still can't figure it out). The handling is really nice, the gas tank holds quite a bit (20 gallons, which is a lot for a sedan). Mechanically, it works very well (I got it 114k miles, it's nearing 200k and runs just as well as the day I got it), and there haven't been many electronic or electrical issues. The window regulators are the only things that are really wrong with it, and the brake light gets loose every now and again. Other than that - best car ever.

1993 Plymouth Colt - This is an odd car, and the one I drove was a manual transmission, but it was quite fun. There was nothing spectacular about it - it got good gas mileage, sure. It wasn't powerful at all. But its turning was responsive. Its engine was a Mitsubishi engine, which is probably why it lasted so long. It was the car I learned to drive a standard on.

2004 Subaru Legacy - These cars handle very well, and work well in snow and ice (they're AWD). A little under-powered for my liking, but overall great cars. Apparently very easy to work on.

Least Favorite:

1987 and 1981 Jaguar XJ6 - The 1987 was my first car, and the 1981 was my second (my mom had a thing for Jaguars). Everything Regular Car Reviews said about them was entirely accurate, and there were no differences between the 1981 and 1987 that I can recall. They're sluggish, riddled with electrical and mechanical problems, HORRIBLE gas mileage (like 18 or so highway), and just overall terrible cars. The 1981 was worse than the 1987 because it had this issue where it would 'lurch' for lack of a better word - I would step on the gas and it wouldn't respond, then throw it all at once, and then nothing. When my car died while I was turning across traffic, that was when my parents decided it was time for a different car, as it was clear that one was going to kill me.

Ford Mustang (newest series) - Fuck, where can I begin? These things make you look like a douche bag. I drove it for all of about 3 to 5 miles, but every stop light, I'd press the gas...nothing...then VOOM. I just wanted to take off lightly, and the car wouldn't let me. Also, what's up with the hood protruding slightly upwards? It bothers me that the windshield allows me to see a bit, but that part of the hood is clearly in the way, and the visibility in it feels very limited. The steering isn't great either.

...

I probably have more that I can think of, but those are the ones that stick out to me.

Best car: 1981 Porsche 911sc coupe with sunroof. Let's hear it for straightforward German engineering. Bottom end of the engine will go 300,000 miles or more if treated right. Leaks a bit of oil, but holds plenty. Fun as fuck to drive. If you know how to service it (which isn't hard to learn) it's fairly easy, forgiving, and doesn't cost much.

Worst: 1974 Porsche 914 2.0. Goddamn hard car to work on. Everything more than changing the air filter requires removing the engine (not really, but close). Leaks like a sieve. Fun as fuck to drive, but lacks power for extended runs above 100mph. Once dumped a shit load of clutch dust on my face. Bleah. Wasn't fun.

Fuck I love Porsche from the 1980s. I have driven about two of those and driving them is straight forward. Driving them with a stick...it really felt like how a manual should be. No play in the clutch. The oil leak I am familiar with as well, or at least the smell of it.

My friend's dad would always fix up old ones, and I got to drive them a few times.

For some reason I've always drifted to Fords. First car was a 77 Mercury Cougar, damn thing would pass anything on the road but a gas station. I've had other cars, Buicks a Chevy or two and a pontiac, not to mention the pair of Caravans I had at different times but my favorite cars I've ever owned were my 99 ZX2 and my 77 Cougar. Today I drive a 2012 Fusion.

Fun on the road my 2000 vow Passat 1.8 turbo 5-speed.

Fun off road 1992 Toyota pickup, easy to work on it too.

Current, 2009 4x4 Chevy duramax truck. I really like the power of diesel. A little harder to work on, though.
Toyota is easy to work with. So are older chevys. But you know what? FUCK Nissan. Fuck those cars right in their tailpipes.

Nissan Leaf wins hands down, and I really love(d) my Hyundai cars. Everything about the Leaf is smooth and easy. After a few lemon cars I have a paranoia about cars breaking down, but without all of those engine noises/power shifting I never catch myself thinking "that's not good".

I am a 2013 Leaf owner as well and I totally agree with you. Once the range on these gets up closer to the 200 mile mark and more charging infrastructure is installed I think a lot more folks will drive electric. I have great hopes for the Tesla Model 3 when it arrives. I'll probably abandon the Leaf for one of those unless their range improves by then.

1996 Porsche 993. Wasn't the fastest but it was so analog and crisp. I loved it.

As far as ease, 80's 90's toyotas are stupid simple.

My answer to both questions is my Audi. It was an '02 3.0 A4. Easily the best feeling car on the road that I've ever owned. It also cost at least twice for any part than most other makes and everything is the engine bay is packed in tight.

I had just finished doing the timing belt ($1200 in parts) when a deer ran into me on the highway and totalled the car. So bittersweet ... I lost a great ride, but also saved thousands in repairs.

My favorite was the 1985 F250 that my father let me use after I got my license. It was built like a tank, vehicles of that era had very little emissions junk bolted on and easy to work on because there was so much room in the engine compartment. I wish it was still running today, because my 1998 Expedition is draining my pocketbook and my sanity with the never-ending series of malfunctions and failures it is experiencing over the last three months. It's like the Ford version of puberty, I think.

Best: 94 Silverado, I could literally sit in the engine bay to work on it.
Worst: 2004 Monte carlo, I had to take off a bunch of stuff to get to anything.
I had a late 90s Kia. It was by no means a "good" car but it was a hilarious little shitbox that would just about rattle your balls off. I never got brave enough to try to exceed 95 in it, though.

Jeep Wrangler...TJ and earlier. God those things are wonderful. I've had one for 11 years and I love it as much today as the day I bought it. There is enough room under the hood to do whatever you need to do and the L6 engine is a great motor to work on.

Are you starting with a clean drive/new machine, or are you installing over a previously encrypted drive? A couple of WS I installed Linux on, required me to run a partition manager to delete the encrypted volumes before I could install the new OS.
